cues.text: This is the Daily Karma. These five minutes are for rest and recovery. Find a position that feels supported. You can sit, or lie down. Let your eyes close, or rest gently on the painting.
Feel the surface beneath you. Let it take a little more of your weight. Soften your jaw. Let your shoulders settle. There is nothing you need to achieve in this moment.
Notice one breath arriving, and one breath leaving. Let your breathing find its own comfortable rhythm. If the breath feels difficult to follow, simply notice the support beneath your hands.
Today, let karma be an invitation to notice intention and action. A small act of care can shape what comes next. For these few minutes, that act is giving yourself room to rest.
Picture a quiet lake beneath the mountains. A ripple moves across the water, then softens. You do not need to smooth the surface. Let each thought arrive, and let it move at its own pace.

Bring your attention to your forehead, your shoulders, and your hands. Notice where effort is gathering. If it feels comfortable, release a little. Rest can begin with one small place becoming softer.
You do not have to earn this pause. Nothing about feeling tired makes you less worthy of care. Let the next breath be ordinary. Let your body be here, without asking it to improve.
For a little while, I will be quiet. Feel the support beneath you. When your attention wanders, return gently. That return is another small act of kindness.
Still here. Still supported. Notice what this moment feels like, even if nothing has changed. There is no particular feeling you need to have.
Choose one gentle action to carry into the day. A slower beginning. A glass of water. A moment before you answer. Let care for yourself shape the care you offer next.
Feel the room around you. Move your fingers when you are ready. Let your eyes open gently. Thank you for resting with Karma.
